title: Each review axis reads one file the team owns

statements.says: Each of the three review axes reads one file of its own in docs/agents/: review-standards.md, review-spec.md and review-architecture.md.
Each review file holds the Plugin's defaults for that axis and the team's own checks.
The smell baseline becomes review-standards.md, and the arrangement baseline becomes review-architecture.md.
Each check says what to look for, whether it is a hard breach or a judgement call, and the paths it covers when it covers fewer than all.
A "Do not report" list names what the axis skips.
A hard breach is always fixed and never left.
A judgement call may be left, with the reason.
A check that should also shape the build is a rule, because a review file is read only by its review.
review-changes' sub-agents each follow one axis skill in a mode that reports and edits nothing.
A breach of a rule marked hard is now always fixed, as a moved name already was.
A team had no good place to add a review check: a new rule loads into every Session, and an item in the smell baseline could never be a hard breach.
code-review is renamed so Claude does not confuse it with Claude Code's own /code-review.
Having review-changes' sub-agents follow the axis skills gives each axis one text, so a review by hand checks what the loop checks.

One file for every review check was rejected, because every axis would read every check, the file would grow with each concern, and Anthropic warns that a long review file weakens the rules that matter most.
One file for each concern, such as review-security.md, was rejected, because every axis would read every file to find its own checks.

A root REVIEW.md that also steers Anthropic's Code Review on a pull request was rejected for now, because up to 2026-09-10 Anthropic's docs said that Code Review reads REVIEW.md as it stands and does not expand an @ import, so a REVIEW.md that imports the team's files would reach the review as one line, and a copy would drift from the three axis files.
Keeping the baselines as separate files was rejected, because the standards axis would read two files for its checks and a team would look in two places to change one review.
Letting code-review keep its own brief for each axis was rejected, because its briefs had already drifted from the loop's axis skills and a review by hand missed checks the loop makes.
